full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE December 10, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information News Desk 907- 428-7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov SEOC Update: 2025 October West Coast Storm – Disaster Update JOINT BASE ELMENDORF RICHARDSON, Alaska — The disaster recovery operation continues to draw down and demobilize, as winter weather has begun to prevent safe air travel and working conditions in the impacted communities. Recovery operations will begin increasing again as weather is more favorable for outdoor work in the springtime. With weather delays occurring, state and FEMA Individual Assistance (IA) teams continue to travel to those impacted communities, to meet with residents, provide assistance with IA applications, and perform damage assessments. Impacted residents are continuing to submit State and FEMA IA applications. As of Dec. 10, 1,920 state and 1,630 FEMA applications for IA have been received. The Disaster Assistance Centers (DACs) located in Anchorage, Bethel, and Kotzebue have closed. There are currently 678 individuals, from 177 households, in non-congregate sheltering (NCS) in Anchorage. To date, more than 42,000 meals have been prepared and delivered to those in NCS. Plans for short-term temporary housing are being finalized, with the goal to transition out of non-congregate housing as soon as possible. The state is continuing to receive assistance with staffing from other states through the Emergency Management Assistance Compact (EMAC). Currently, there are 10 people from five states that are deployed to Alaska in response to the declared disaster. Temporary Housing Mission Temporary Housing units are being furnished this week. The goal is to move non- congregate shelter residents into these units as quickly as possible. To date, the Mass Care team has received keys to apartments and is coordinating with ready applicants for their move-in. The team is also facilitating the apartment leasing process, providing transportation for residents and their belongings, and supplying welcome kits that include essential items like paper products and cleaning supplies. USPS Mail Delivery The Post Offices in Kipnuk and Kwigillingok remain closed. Mail delivery for Kipnuk and Kwigillingok will be cooped at Midtown Station, located at 3721 B Street in Anchorage. 2 Mail forwarding is active, and some residents have submitted change-of-address requests. Alaska SNAP Update The Division of Public Assistance (DPA) has been granted a Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) “hot foods waiver”. The waiver allows individuals and families receiving SNAP benefits to use their Quest (EBT) Card to buy pre-cooked foods, such as rotisserie chicken, soup, or hot deli meals from SNAP-authorized grocery and convenience stores statewide. All other SNAP rules remain the same. This waiver is in place through December 20th but may be extended if necessary. For more information on SNAP, go to the Alaska DPA website. Donations collection warehouse closed The donations collection warehouse in Anchorage, provided by Chugach Electric Association at 1120 East 1st Avenue, has closed and is no longer accepting donations. Individuals desiring to make donations to benefit the impacted residents are encouraged to give financially through established relief organizations such as the Alaska Community Foundation, American Red Cross of Alaska, Salvation Army, Alaska Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster, and Team Rubicon. Claim Pets Deadline The Office of the State Veterinarian and partners have successfully reunited approximately 125 dogs with their families following Typhoon Halong. However, nearly 20 dogs remain unclaimed, and time is running out. The Deadline is December 15, 2025. If you or someone you know is missing a pet from the storm, you must take action before this date. full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE November 5, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information News Desk 907- 428-7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov SEOC Update: 2025 October West Coast Storm – Disaster Update JOINT BASE ELMENDORF RICHARDSON, Alaska — A Major Disaster Declaration has been signed by President Trump in response to a state-declared disaster, for the 2025 October West Coast Storms, including Typhoon Halong and related storms. The State Emergency Operations Center (SEOC) is coordinating with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to transition from a state-led response to a joint, long-term recovery operation through a Unified Command. The primary focus is life sustainment and stabilization for the impacted area. Recovery is a priority for the impacted areas, and recovery operations continue with an emphasis on restoring critical infrastructure and services – including water, power, and communications, and emergency home and boardwalk repairs. Coordination between federal, state, local and tribal partners is continuing to provide critical supplies to impacted communities and address community needs as they are reported. As of this afternoon, 1,321 applications for state Individual Assistance (IA) have been received. FEMA has received 623 IA applications to date. State IA and FEMA IA are coordinating to share information and encourage applicants to register for each program. All individuals residing in congregate shelters in Anchorage and Bethel have transitioned to non-congregate sheltering, some shelters will remain in standby status for the coming days to accept potential evacuees. The Egan Civic and Convention Center shelter will close today, marking its final day of operations. Beginning November 5, shelter services will transition to the Spenard Community Recreation Center, located at 2020 W 48th Ave, Anchorage, AK 99517. The facility will be open daily from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. The Spenard Community Recreation Center will provide temporary shelter for individuals displaced by the 2025 October West Coast Storm and will serve as a short- term pass-through location as survivors move into the non-congregate sheltering program. 2 A total of 577 individuals have transitioned from congregate to non-congregate sheltering in Anchorage. Anchorage Disaster Assistance Center (DAC) A DAC will be operating at the Calista Corporation Building located at 1400 W. Benson Blvd, Suite 110, Anchorage, AK. The DAC will be open November 3 – 14, 2025, Monday – Friday 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Bethel Disaster Assistance Center (DAC) A DAC will be operating at the AVCP Tugkar Building located at 570 3rd Ave, Bethel, AK. To donate new items, bring them to Team Rubicon at the Chugach Electric Warehouse located at 1120 East 1st Avenue, Anchorage, AK, daily from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Team Rubicon is asking that donors send their donations to the warehouse, not hand deliver them. They also recommend that people and organizations wanting to contribute to the long-term recovery of survivors donate monetarily to reputable organizations such as Team 3 Rubicon https://teamrubiconusa.org/ or the The Alaska Community Foundation https://alaskacf.org/. A list of resources related to the disaster is available at ready.alaska.gov, under Top News. Survivors are also encouraged to visit Alaska Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster (VOAD) for additional resources https://www.akvoad.org/. All donations, events, and services available for survivors of the 2025 October West Coast Storm should be directed to storm2025@ready.alaska.gov. AKOM is assisting the Division of Forestry & Fire Protection with winterization, debris removal, muck-outs and supporting cargo flights. American Red Cross: The Red Cross continues to support the recovery by providing assistance with IA registrations, non-congregate housing, and Red Cross Individual Assistance. Association of Village Council Presidents (AVCP): AVCP is working to develop a plan for the transition to long-term recovery, managed by AVCP. There are still many survivors from the affected villages with unidentified needs. Team Rubicon encourages anyone in the Y-K Delta with remaining needs due to the storm to email familyrequest@avcp.org. Team Rubicon is working alongside the AVCP. This email will help volunteers in Bethel fulfill these requests and AVCP get the items needed to those who need them. The Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC): DEC is working closely with communities, local governments, tribal and regional organizations, and state and federal partners to support recovery efforts in Western Alaska. This live website provides daily updates on the status of drinking water, wastewater, solid waste, and environmental conditions in affected communities: https://dec.alaska.gov/commish/west-coast-alaska-storm-response-2025/ U.S. Postal Service (USPS): Mail delivery continues to be available at the USPS Egan Center Mail Unit for residents of Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. Pickup is available daily between 1:00 p.m. and 4 p.m. daily. Individuals are encouraged by USPS to complete a Change of Address (COA) request, to prevent an interruption in mail delivery. full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Feb, 12 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: Jeremy Zidek, 907-428-7077, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.Gov Rural Resiliency Workshop to be Held in Bethel, Alaska in February 2025 JOINT BASE ELMENDORF-RICHARDSON, Alaska This February, the Association of Village Council Presidents (AVCP) and the Alaska Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management (DHS&EM) will partner to host a Rural Resiliency Workshop in Bethel, Alaska. The three-day event, February 25–27, 2025, will bring representatives from 13 communities across the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta to Bethel to learn vital skills related to disaster preparedness and response. Topics covered will include disaster response options, past disaster impacts, grants, rural law enforcement, shelter operations, oil spill response, and more. “Increasing regional public safety and emergency response coordination and preparedness is a top priority for AVCP. We are excited to partner with DHS&EM on these workshops that support our Tribe’s emergency preparedness. In addition, we are also very pleased to offer public safety officer emergency response training for TPO/VPO and VPSOs as part of this week’s activities,” said Vivian Korthuis, AVCP’s CEO. The workshop will host three members from each of the 13 communities, including one local law enforcement officer (Tribal Police Officer or Village Police Officer). AVCP’s Village Public Safety Officers (VPSO) from around the region will also be in attendance. VPSOs/VPOs and TPOs play a critical role in disaster response by liaising with city and tribal leadership to ensure the safety of residents. Including local and regional law enforcement officers in the Rural Resiliency Workshop will foster closer collaboration among community leaders and emergency responders before, during, and after disaster events. “Throughout the years, AVCP and DHS&EM have worked together during the response and recovery phases of many disasters,” said Bryan Fisher, Director of DHS&EM. “AVCP has provided supplies to disaster-impacted communities, supported shelters both in communities and in Bethel, provided transportation to and from impacted areas, enhanced law enforcement presence, and helped restore critical infrastructure. This workshop expands our partnership to focus on the pre-disaster preparedness phase.” A key component of the workshop will be a tabletop exercise, where participants will explore the steps communities can take before, during, and after a severe coastal storm—such as the 2022 Typhoon Merbok that impacted all the invited communities. In addition, participants will discuss the disaster declaration process and review disaster recovery programs that help individuals and communities recover after a disaster. DHS&EM will also work with communities to update their Small Community Emergency Response Plans, customized flipbooks that contain essential, community-specific information for responding to the first 72 hours of a disaster. DHS&EM typically conducts Rural Resiliency Workshops in different locations each year to reach communities across Alaska. However, the workshop will return to Bethel in the fall of 2025 to assist an additional 11–13 coastal communities in preparing for coastal sea storms. Media Contact: Jeremy Zidek, 907-428-7077, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.Gov ###

full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE October 21, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: Public Information Officer Jeremy Zidek 907-441-2337, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov 2025 West Coast Storm Disaster Housing Task Force Established JOINT BASE ELMENDORF RICHARDSON, Alaska — The State Emergency Operations Center (SEOC), in cooperation with the Alaska Housing Finance Corporation, Southcentral Foundation, Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium, Municipality of Anchorage, Cook Inlet Housing Authority, The Association of Village Council Presidents Regional Housing Authority, Rasmuson Foundation, and other state, local, and tribal partners have established a State of Alaska Disaster Housing Task Force to address immediate housing needs related to the 2025 October West Coast Storm. "The state and Alaska Housing Finance Corporation is leading the West Coast Storm Housing Force. The goal is to work with all partners to get evacuees out of group shelters and into better accommodations, in some cases longer-term temporary housing," said Governor Mike Dunleavy. "Right now, storm survivors are being matched with housing options. We are also working to fix homes so those who can return to their community will be able to do so." The mission of the Disaster Housing Task Force is to identify housing and match those facilities with disaster survivors. Housing options included non-congregate shelters like hotel rooms, dormitories, or other units with greater privacy. A mix of housing options could be used to address short, intermediate, and long-term needs. The State's Individual Assistance program includes a Temporary Housing program which can provide homeowners with 18 months and renters with 3 months of housing assistance. The Housing Task Force is assembling a list of available housing units and landlord contact information. This inventory list will be used to pair those registered with housing needs and appropriate, available housing stock. "While our goal is to get people back into their homes and communities as fast as possible that may not be possible before winter sets in," said Director Bryan Fisher, Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management. "When we can't get people back home, we will look at the needs of each IA applicant and match them with a housing option." full_text: PRESS RELEASE March 26, 2026 By Jeremy Zidek Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: Jeremy Zidek, 907-428-7077 Governor Dunleavy Declares Northwest Arctic Borough Extreme Cold Utility Disruption a Disaster JOINT BASE ELMENDORF-RICHARDSON, Alaska — Governor Mike Dunleavy has issued a state disaster declaration in response to widespread utility disruption caused by extreme cold across the Northwest Arctic Borough. The declaration activates the State of Alaska Public Assistance program, providing essential funding to restore damaged critical infrastructure to pre-disaster conditions. Over the past several months, sustained extreme cold has pushed local infrastructure to its breaking point. In multiple communities, utility providers have struggled to maintain power and keep water and sewer systems operational. The communities of Selawik, Shungnak, Ambler, and Buckland have all experienced significant freeze-ups in their water and sewer systems, which now require extensive thawing and permanent repairs. Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Director Bryan Fisher stated that the communities and the Northwest Arctic Borough have done everything possible with the resources and personnel available to keep these systems online. He noted that with this declaration, the state will be able to reimburse communities for emergency protective measures, assist with the utility restoration effort, and fund permanent repair projects. The state Public Assistance program is designed to restore critical infrastructure such as buildings, roads, utilities, bridges, and communications to a pre-disaster condition. Local jurisdictions, tribal organizations, and certain non-profits with documented disaster damages may be eligible to apply for Public Assistance disaster recovery grants. ### Media Contact: Jeremy Zidek, 907-428-7077, Jeremy.Zidek@alaska.gov

full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE October 15, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: Public Information Officer Jeremy Zidek 907-441-2337, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov SEOC Update: 2025 October West Coast Storm – Situation Update JOINT BASE ELMENDORF RICHARDSON, Alaska — The State Emergency Operations Center (SEOC) activation level has moved to level 4 – Major Incident Response, Alaska SEOC’s highest level. As rescues were completed, and impacted communities reported accountability, SEOC’s priority now is life sustainment, shelter operations, and interim restoration of community water, power, sanitation, and medical services. The Alaska State Troopers have notified next of kin that 67-year-old Ella Mae Kashatok has been located deceased. The remaining two missing people from Kwigillingok have been identified as Vernon Pavil, 71 and Chester Kashatok, 41. The entire SEOC inter- agency staff grieves this loss of Alaskans. Troopers are requesting that anyone who knows of additional people who are unaccounted for, please contact the Alaska State Troopers at 907-451-5100. The Troopers will continue to coordinate with the local community to continue recovery efforts for the two missing individuals. The SEOC, in cooperation with multiple state, local, and volunteer agencies, has initiated an evacuation of the residents currently sheltered in Kipnuk and Kwigillingok whose homes were destroyed. As sheltering capacity was reached in Bethel, hundreds of survivors are being relocated outside the region to safe, warm shelters elsewhere within the state. The Alaska National Guard is supporting the evacuation using its tactical airlift capabilities. Two UH-60 Blackhawks, one HH-60 MEDEVAC, one CH-47 Chinook, and a C-17 Globemaster III are carrying out this mission. Today, Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta region disaster survivors, whose homes were destroyed, are being flown to Bethel via Alaska Air Guard helicopters and then transferred to a C-17 for transport to shelter in Anchorage. The American Red Cross is coordinating the sheltering and food service response once in Anchorage. Additional support in this effort is being provided by the Municipality of Anchorage, Department of Health and Social services, University of Alaska, and other local volunteer organizations. Additional survivor evacuations will be ongoing based on survivor need, and will use multiple contract, commercial, and National Guard aircraft. 2 The Alaska Rescue Coordination Center has reported receiving an overwhelming number of calls for non-critical evacuations. The SEOC is requesting calls for non- critical evacuations be made to your local community or Yukon Kuskokwim Health Corporation. For life-threatening emergencies please contact the Alaska Rescue Coordination Center at 907-551-7230. The SEOC currently has emergency management specialists deployed to Bethel and Kotzebue to coordinate state disaster response in each region. The Alaska Organized Militia has more than 100 deployed personnel across the state in support of the response. SEOC has received mutual aid from other states through the Emergency Management Assistance Compact including Colorado, Virgina, South Carolina, Texas and Arkansas. For those wishing to make donations, cash donations are preferred and are accepted through the Alaska Community Foundation’s Western Alaska Disaster Relief Fund. Additional information can be found at: https://alaskacf.org. The American Red Cross has brought additional staff from around the nation to help in Anchorage and Bethel to assist with sheltering and other mass care needs. The World Central Kitchen has arrived and is coordinating feeding of the survivors in shelters. The Salvation Army is supporting mass care and working to coordinate donation management and sheltering needs. As of this morning, DHS&EM has received 230 applications for Individual Assistance. Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta Damage assessments for impacted communities is ongoing in coordination with DOT&PF, AVCP, and ANTHC. Bethel – Over 100 people were sheltered in Bethel overnight at the Alaska National Guard Armory. Other communities in the region are sheltering individuals in smaller numbers at local schools or community buildings. The YKHC, World Central Kitchen, and American Red Cross are supporting sheltering needs in Bethel. The Brown Slough Bridge has been assessed and reopened. Kipnuk –The runway in Kipnuk has been reopened. Currently, the council building and school have power and are running on generators. The remainder of the community is without power. Communication has been reestablished with the community through Starlink. GCI is sending a technician to Kipnuk, working to restore cell service. Significant damage to the cemetery has been reported. Kwigillingok – 350 people were sheltered overnight. Last night, an SEOC emergency management specialist was able to travel to the community aboard an Alaska National Guard Blackhawk to deliver a pallet of water and support communications. VPSO’s in the community have received Starlink and communications have been reestablished. Water pressure has been restored at the water plant and washeteria. Assessments are continuing for damages to the community’s sewer system. Restrooms at the school are 3 working. Damage to many homes is severe, and the community leadership is instructing residents not to reenter homes due to safety concerns. Quinhagak – 10 Alaska State Defense Force deployed. There is a DEC Remote Maintenance Worker on site working to make repairs to the water infrastructure and assess further damage. Nightmute – A spill was reported in Nightmute. DEC responded and assessed it is diesel from heating tanks and limited to 35 gallons. Sorbent materials were sent to Nightmute and are being used to address the spill. Norton Sound/Nome Impacts to the Norton Sound and Nome area were not severe. Approximately half of Elim is still without power. The city is working with the Alaska Village Electric Cooperative to restore power. There is minor damage to Moses Point Road. Service members from the Alaska Organized Militia remain on State Active Duty in Nome to continue support for disaster response and recovery. Northwest Arctic Borough/Kotzebue The SEOC has two emergency management specialists in Kotzebue to assist the NWAB and City of Kotzebue with resource needs as they develop. Last night there were no people sheltered overnight in Kotzebue. Kotzebue – The Alaska Organized Militia (AKOM) has 9 members deployed to Kotzebue. 132 homes have been inspected, and 52 are reported as damaged. AKOM has begun muck out and dry out of many homes. 23 homes remain in the flood area and have not been inspected. Kivalina – No one at the shelter at this time. Damage assessment is ongoing. State of Alaska Individual Assistance Disaster survivors in the designated disaster area can register for the state's Individual Assistance program by visiting the DHS&EM registration webpage at [https://ready.alaska.gov/ia] (https://ready.alaska.gov/ia). Telephone registration is available at 1-844-445-7131. The State's Individual Assistance (IA) program is designed to provide financial assistance to individuals or families for damage to a primary residence, primary mode of transportation, essential personal property, and medical/funeral/dental needs created as a direct result of a declared disaster. The SEOC understand that one of the most heartbreaking decisions people had to make during this disaster was leaving their pets behind. For many, animals are beloved members of the family, and being forced to evacuate without them adds another layer of stress and grief to an already overwhelming situation. Safety and survival often require impossible choices in moments like these, and we want every pet owner to know that their love and concern for their animals has not gone unnoticed. At this time evacuation of people is the priority. 4 The state’s Mass Care Task Force and our partner agencies, including the Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation State Veterinarian’s Office, are actively working to coordinate rescue efforts for stranded and displaced animals. Every effort is being made to reunite families with their animals safely and as quickly as possible. ### Media Contact: Public Information Officer Jeremy Zidek 907-441-2337, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov

full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE November 10, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information News Desk 907- 428-7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov SEOC Update: 2025 October West Coast Storm – Disaster Update JOINT BASE ELMENDORF RICHARDSON, Alaska — A Major Disaster Declaration has been signed by President Trump in response to a state-declared disaster, for the 2025 October West Coast Storms, including Typhoon Halong and related storms. Governor Mike Dunleavy has signed an extension of the Disaster Declaration for the October 2026 West Coast Storms. The 30-day extension ensures that ongoing recovery operations can continue without interruption, allowing responders and partner agencies to complete as much work as possible before winter freeze-up conditions limit access in the region. The original disaster declaration was set to expire on November 9, 2025. The State Emergency Operations Center (SEOC) continues coordinating with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to transition from a state-led response to a joint, long-term recovery operation through a Unified Command. The primary focus is life sustainment and stabilization for the impacted area. Recovery is a priority for the impacted areas, and recovery operations continue with an emphasis on restoring critical infrastructure and services – including water, power, and communications, and emergency home and boardwalk repairs. Coordination between federal, state, local and tribal partners is continuing to provide critical supplies to impacted communities and address community needs as they are reported. As of this afternoon, 1,440 applications for state Individual Assistance (IA) have been received. FEMA has received 786 IA applications to date. State IA and FEMA IA are coordinating to share information and encourage applicants to register for each program. All individuals residing in congregate shelters in Anchorage and Bethel have transitioned to direct non-congregate sheltering. Survivors currently in Anchorage can register for long-term, temporary housing through the Non-Congregate Shelter (NCS) Program by calling 907-759-6927, Monday through Saturday, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Survivors located outside Anchorage should contact the Yukon-Kuskokwim Health Corporation (YKHC) Travel Line at 833-543-6625 (option 1) for assistance traveling 2 to Anchorage for placement in the NCS program. Individuals will first travel to Bethel to complete registration before continuing on to Anchorage, where lodging will be provided. Upon arrival in Anchorage, the American Red Cross will meet survivors at the airport, provide transportation to NCS hotels or other locations as needed, and offer additional care and support services. A total of 614 individuals have transitioned to non-congregate sheltering in Anchorage. Plans for longer-term temporary housing are currently in development. Some survivors may be sheltering with neighbors, family, or friends; it is crucial that those who are affected by the recent storms register for both state and federal IA programs and other forms of assistance. State of Alaska Individual Assistance (IA) – Deadline is December 9, 2025 To register for State of Alaska Individual Assistance: Call 1-844-445-7131, Monday – Friday, 8 a.m. – 4 p.m. Or apply online https://ready.alaska.gov/Recovery/IA FEMA Individual Assistance (IA) – Deadline is December 22, 2025 To register for FEMA Individual Assistance: Call 1-866-342-1699, Monday – Sunday, 9 a.m. – 6:30 p.m. Or apply online at https://disasterassistance.gov Small Business Administration (SBA) – Deadline is December 22, 2025 SBA offers low interest, long-term disaster loans to homeowners, renters, businesses, and private nonprofits to repair and replace property destroyed by the storms. Call 1-800- 659-2955, Monday – Friday 6 a.m. – 4 p.m. Or apply online at https://sba.gov/disaster Disaster Assistance Centers (DACs) are now open and providing in-person support for survivors in Anchorage, Bethel and Kotzebue. Anchorage Disaster Assistance Center (DAC) A DAC will be operating at the Calista Corporation Building located at 1400 W. Benson Blvd, Suite 110-155, Anchorage, AK. The DAC will be open through November 14, 2025, Monday – Friday 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Please note this DAC will be closed in observance of Veterans Day on Tuesday 11/11/2025. Bethel Disaster Assistance Center (DAC) A DAC will be operating at the AVCP Tugkar Building located at 570 3rd Ave, Bethel, AK. The DAC will be open through November 14, 2025, Monday – Friday 10:00 a.m.– 12:00 p.m. and 1:00 p.m. – 4 p.m. Kotzebue Disaster Assistance Center (DAC) A DAC will be operating at the Maniilaq Health Center’s Ferguson Building located at 733 2nd Avenue, Kotzebue, AK. The DAC will be open today through November 14, 2025, Monday – Friday 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. 3 Alaska 211 can connect individuals with available local resources that best fit their needs. Call 2-1-1 or 1-800-478-2221. Email: alaska211@ak.org or visit www.Alaska211.org. Native Alaskan language interpretation services are available. Team Rubicon is coordinating the collection of new items only for donations. To donate new items, bring them to Team Rubicon at the Chugach Electric Warehouse located at 1120 East 1st Avenue, Anchorage, AK, daily from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Team Rubicon is asking that donors send their donations to the warehouse, not hand deliver them. They also recommend that people and organizations wanting to contribute to the long-term recovery of survivors donate monetarily to reputable organizations such as Team Rubicon https://teamrubiconusa.org/ or the The Alaska Community Foundation https://alaskacf.org/. A list of resources related to the disaster is available at ready.alaska.gov, under Top News. Survivors are also encouraged to visit Alaska Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster (VOAD) for additional resources https://www.akvoad.org/. All donations, events, and services available for survivors of the 2025 October West Coast Storm should be directed to storm2025@ready.alaska.gov. Interagency Partner Operations Alaska Organized Militia (AKOM): There are 78 AKOM members activated on State Active Duty with additional authorization as needed for disaster response. AKOM is assisting the Division of Forestry & Fire Protection with winterization, debris removal, muck-outs and supporting cargo flights. American Red Cross: The Red Cross continues to support the recovery by providing assistance with IA registrations, non-congregate housing, and Red Cross Individual Assistance. Association of Village Council Presidents (AVCP): AVCP is working to develop a plan for the transition to long-term recovery, managed by AVCP. There are still many survivors from the affected villages with unidentified needs. Team Rubicon is working alongside the AVCP and encourages anyone in the Y-K Delta with remaining needs due to the storm to email familyrequest@avcp.org.This email will help volunteers in Bethel fulfill these requests and AVCP get the items needed to those who need them. The Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC): DEC is working closely with communities, local governments, tribal and regional organizations, and state and federal partners to support recovery efforts in Western Alaska. This live website provides daily updates on the status of drinking water, wastewater, solid waste, and environmental conditions in affected communities: https://dec.alaska.gov/commish/west-coast-alaska-storm-response-2025/ ### Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information News Desk 907- 428-7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov

full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE November 19, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information News Desk 907-428- 7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov State Individual Disaster Declaration deadline extended until January 8, 2026, for 2025 West Coast Storm JOINT BASE ELMENDORF RICHARDSON, Alaska — The State of Alaska has extended the Individual Assistance (IA) registration deadline until January 8, 2026. This will give those impacted by the storm additional time to register for this state program. 1702 individuals and families have registered for State IA as of Nov. 19, 2025. The State of Alaska IA program is designed to help individuals with Housing Assistance (HA), Other Needs Assistance (ONA) and Temporary Housing Grants (THG). Residents within the Kashunamiut, Lower Yukon, Yupitt, Pribilof Island, Iditarod area, Lower Kuskokwim and Bering Strait Regional Educational Attendance Areas (REAA), Yukon- Koyukuk REAA, the City of Galena, as well as the Northwest Arctic (NWAB) and North Slope Borough (NSB) are eligible of State IA. HA assistance is available to homeowners to repair disaster-related damage not covered by insurance or by other governmental ﬁnancial assistance resources. If insurance covers damages, applicant may be eligible for reimbursement of the deductible. ONA expenses (not covered by insurance or by other ﬁnancial assistance resources) may include the lesser of the costs to clean, repair or replace essential personal property items identiﬁed on the program eligible property list. State IA can provide assistance for subsistence structures and other needs not met by other assistance programs. THG assistance provides ﬁnancial assistance when an eligible applicant’s primary residence is rendered uninhabitable due to a declared disaster. Individuals must apply for state Individual Assistance (IA) within the registration window of October 9, 2025 – January 8, 2026. Apply online at https://ready.alaska.gov/IA or call 844- 445-7131. In addition, federal disaster recovery assistance is available. FEMA IA: www.DisasterAssistance.gov FEMA Hotline: 1-866-342-1699 Small Business Administration: https://sba.gov/disaster or call 1-800- 659-2955 ### Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information News Desk 907-428- 7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov

Yup’ik Language Tool Supports Behavioral Health Understanding Moses Marr’aq Wiseman, a Yup’ik speaker from Chefornak, recently supported evacuees from Western Alaska by providing Yup’ik interpretation at Anchorage shelters, using a newly developed glossary of behavioral health terms. Having culturally appropriate language available, he said, helped ease conversations and made it easier for people to understand and talk about their experiences. Wiseman, who serves as Alaska Native Languages Program Director at the Alaska Institute for Justice, helped launch the free, online Yup’ik behavioral health glossary last month. The resource allows users to search health-related terms, see Yup’ik translations, and hear correct pronunciation. Funded by a grant from the Alaska Department of Health, the glossary was developed over several years through collaboration with Yup’ik speakers, interpreters, and medical professionals. Project leaders emphasized that the glossary is a “living” resource that will continue to evolve as language and community needs change. The resource is available at: https://www.akijp.org/yugtun-medical-resources/ Moses Marr'aq Wiseman and Indra Arriaga with the Alaska Institute for Justice on Nov. 6, 2025. Through the ANTHC Behavioral Health Wellness Clinic, individuals can access behavioral health assessments, health behavior coaching, individual and group counseling, and referrals to additional resources or treatments. All services are available via telehealth, allowing patients to receive care from home. The Behavioral Health Wellness Clinic is designed to support overall wellness but is not a crisis service. If you are experiencing a medical emergency, call 911. If you or someone you know is in a mental health crisis, call or text the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 for immediate support. For more information or to learn how to access services, visit the ANTHC Behavioral Health Wellness Clinic webpage at: https://anthc.org/patient-care/bhwc/ January is Mental Wellness Month - Behavioral and Mental Health Services Available Don’t Miss Out on Help - Deadlines Extended for Financial Assistance Disaster Unemployment Assistance Deadline Extended to February 20 If you were impacted by Typhoon Halong and are unable to work due to storm-related damage, Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) is still available. Weekly assistance ranges from $153 to $370 and may be available for up to 27 weeks. To apply, call (907) 465-4691 and ask for Disaster Unemployment Assistance. Interpreter services are available at no cost. full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE November 5, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information News Desk 907- 428-7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov Introduction of Direct to Non-Congregate Sheltering Program JOINT BASE ELMENDORF RICHARDSON, Alaska — Displaced survivors of Typhoon Halong now have access to safe, secure lodging and continued support through the Direct to NCS (Non-Congregate Shelter) Program. This program allows eligible individuals and families to move directly into hotels in Anchorage, bypassing mass congregate sheltering. The program provides survivors with accommodation, meals, and other essential services as recovery efforts continue. All survivors entering the NCS program must apply for State and FEMA Individual Assistance before completing intake into NCS. Survivors can register for the Direct to NCS program in one of the following three ways: NCS Contact Center: Survivors staying in the Anchorage area can contact the NCS Contact Center to register for the program. The contact center can be reached at 907- 759-6927 and will receive registrations over the phone. Yukon Kuskokwim Health Corporation (YKHC) Travel Line: Survivors outside of Anchorage can contact the YKHC Travel Line for assistance in relocating to a hotel room in Anchorage. Survivors will first travel to Bethel for registration and then continue onto Anchorage where they will receive lodging. To arrange travel into Anchorage for the NCS program contact the YKHC Travel Line: 833-543-6625, option 1. Anchorage Disaster Assistance Center (DAC): Survivors in the Anchorage area can sign up in person at the DAC Monday, November 3 to November 14. The DAC is open Monday – Friday 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. at the Calista Corporation Maani Building – 1400 W. Benson Blvd, Suite 110, Anchorage. The American Red Cross will welcome survivors at the airport, provide transportation to NCS hotels from the airport or other Anchorage location, and offer other care and support services. For more information about the Direct to NCS program or assistance with the registration process, please call the NCS Call Center at 907-759-6927. 2 State of Alaska Individual Assistance (IA) To register for State of Alaska Individual Assistance: Call 1-844-445-7131, Monday – Friday, 8 a.m. – 4 p.m. Or apply online https://ready.alaska.gov/Recovery/IA FEMA Individual Assistance (IA) To register for FEMA Individual Assistance: Call 1-866-342-1699, Monday – Sunday, 9 a.m. – 6 p.m. Or apply online at https://disasterassistance.gov ### Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information News Desk 907- 428-7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov

full_text: Media contact: Dana Rosso, 907-428-6039, dana.rosso@alaska.gov, or AKNGpublicaffairs@alaska.gov FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 25-059 October 11, 2025 Alaska National Guard requested to provide additional support for West Coast Storm response JOINT BASE ELMENDORF-RICHARDSON, Alaska – The Alaska National Guard has been requested by the State Emergency Operation Center to provide additional support for the ongoing response to the storms impacting Alaska’s West Coast, including opening the Kotzebue, Bethel and Nome Armories and preparing personnel for deployment to affected communities. The Alaska Organized Militia, which includes the Alaska National Guard, Alaska State Defense Force, and Alaska Naval Militia, has been requested to activate up to 60 members to assist with storm response operations across affected western Alaska communities. Three additional members will augment the SEOC with mass care operations and remote community communications. Personnel will be deployed as needed based on community impact assessments and mission requirements coordinated through the State Emergency Operation Center. Two Alaska Organized Militia members residing in Kotzebue were previously activated under state active-duty orders on October 10 to support local emergency response efforts in coordination with the SEOC and community officials. The armories in Kotzebue, Bethel and Nome will provide evacuation and responder sheltering as the powerful storm system moving across Western Alaska continues to impact coastal regions. The National Weather Service has forecasted coastal flooding, heavy surf, and wind gusts approaching 100 miles per hour along portions of Alaska’s West Coast. Deployed AKOM members have been requested to conduct reconnaissance and reporting of storm damage, debris and water removal, assist with shelter and mass care operations, support local emergency operations centers, and distribute disaster relief supplies. Air and ground transportation assets have also been requested to move personnel and materials as conditions allow. The Alaska National Guard Joint Operations Center will continue coordinating directly with the Incident Commander and the State Emergency Operation Center, monitoring storm conditions and adjusting response operations as needed to support the affected communities. ###

full_text: For Immediate Release May 16, 2022 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: SEOC PIO, 907-428-7140, cell 907-441-2337 Press Release: State of Alaska Individual Assistance provides disaster recovery grants to those impacted by 2022 Spring Floods Individuals and families can now apply for state disaster recovery grants JOINT BASE ELMENDORF-RICHARDSON, Alaska — Governor Mike Dunleavy declared the 2022 Spring Floods a disaster on May 7, 2022, in response to ice jam flooding on the Tanana River in Manley Hot Springs. On May 13, Governor Dunleavy added additional communities to his declaration who also experienced ice jam and snowmelt flooding. The Governor’s declaration activates the state’s Individual Assistance (IA) program which is designed to help individuals and families with damages and/or expenses related to the disaster event. Residents of the Yukon – Koyukuk Regional Education Attendance Area (REAA) including Manley Hot Springs,the Kuspuk REAA (Village of Sleetmute and the Village of Red Devil), the Copper River REAA (Glennallen), and the Iditarod REAA (City of McGrath), are eligible to apply for State Individual Assistance. Disaster survivors can register for the State Individual Assistance program by visiting the Alaska Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management webpage beginning on May 18, 2022 at Ready.Alaska.Gov. Registration opens May 18, 2022 at www.Ready.Alaska.Gov Disaster Assistance Hotline (907) 428-7072 or (907) 428-7075 Registration Deadline July 12, 2022 The State of Alaska IA program has three parts; Temporary Housing grants; Housing Assistance grants; Other Needs Assistance grants. Temporary Housing can provide funds to secure lodging while applicants pursue permanent housing solutions. Financial assistance may be available for up to 18 months for owners and three months for renters. Housing Assistance grants can provide funds for damages to primary residences not covered by insurance. The residence must be owner-occupied at the time of the event. The IA program does not help with secondary homes, recreational properties or homes lived in fewer than six months a year. Damages must be serious and negatively impact the essential living spaces in the home, and damages must be from the declared event. Other Needs Assistance can provide funds for losses to essential personal property not covered by insurance such as clothing, appliances and furniture. It may also reimburse for costs such as clean up and some storage expenses. This assistance may also help with disaster-caused medical/funeral expenses not covered by insurance. Based on damages and eligibility, the maximum grant amount an applicant can receive through Housing Assistance is $18,950, and separately, an additional $18,950 for Other Needs Assistance. Temporary Housing is calculated separately based on family size and local rates of stay. The State of Alaska is working with federal partners to identify programs that may become available to disaster survivors. If activated, federal disaster assistance must be pursued before a State IA award. More IA information can be found at http://ready.alaska.gov/Recovery/IndividualAssistance ###

full_text: PRESS RELEASE January 10, 2025 By Jeremy Zidek Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: Jeremy Zidek, 907-441-2337, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.Gov Governor Dunleavy Declares 2026 Jan Southeast Winter Storm a Disaster JOINT BASE ELMENDORF-RICHARDSON, Alaska — Governor Mike Dunleavy has issued a disaster declaration in response to a series of severe winter storms impacting Southeast Alaska. This action activates the state’s Public Assistance program to support communities as they continue to respond and recover from record-breaking snowfall, extreme cold, and rain. The declaration was made for the City and Borough of Juneau and the City of Hoonah on January 6. Based on impacts across the region the disaster declaration has been expanded and now identifies the City and Borough of Juneau, City of Hoonah, Chatham Regional Education Attendance Area, Haines Borough, and Municipality of Skagway Borough as areas eligible for State of Alaska Public Assistance. From December 2025 through early January 2026, the City and Borough of Juneau (CBJ), and other areas of Southeast Alaska, faced relentless winter conditions that resulted in collapsed roofs, blocked storm drains, and sunken vessels. Local snow management resources were quickly overwhelmed, and local leaders remain concerned about heightened avalanche risks and upcoming weather forecasts. CBJ issued an evacuation advisory and opened an emergency shelter to provide shelter for people who resided in the risk areas. CBJ and the Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes of Alaska officials jointly requested a disaster declaration on January 6 to sustain ongoing response efforts in the Juneau area. That same day the City of Hoonah declared a local disaster and requested assistance. Governor Dunleavy responded immediately, authorizing state recovery programs. Bryan Fisher, Director of the Alaska Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management, praised local leaders for their proactive response and noted that the declaration ensures the state can now provide essential financial support and additional resources. The State Emergency Operation (SEOC) deployed an Emergency Management Specialist to Juneau on January 8 to coordinate state-level assistance and identify immediate needs. Also, the SEOC has raised its activation level to 2 based upon increased risk to Southeast Alaska. In addition, the Department of Transportation and Public Facilities sent more heavy equipment operators to the region to bolster snow removal and avalanche forecasting. To further alleviate the snow management burden on the city, the Department of Environmental Conservation is permitting the disposal of uncontaminated snow into the Gastineau Channel. The Public Assistance program focuses on restoring vital infrastructure, including roads, utilities, and communications systems, to their original condition. Under this declaration, local 2 jurisdictions, tribal organizations, and specific non-profits may be eligible for grants to reimburse the costs of emergency protective measures and infrastructure repairs. ### Media Contact: Jeremy Zidek, 907-441-2337, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.Gov

full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE October 25, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: Public Information Officer News Desk 907-428-7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov SEOC Update: 2025 October West Coast Storm – Disaster Update JOINT BASE ELMENDORF RICHARDSON, Alaska — The State Emergency Operations Center (SEOC) remains at Level 4 – Major Incident Response. The SEOC is coordinating a state led, federally supported, and locally executed effort in the response and recovery to the 2025 West Coast Storms. The Request for Assistance that was submitted by Governor Dunleavy to President Trump, has been approved and a Major Disaster Declaration has been made. This declaration grants access to the federal Individual Assistance (IA) and Public Assistance (PA) programs for the following areas: Lower Kuskokwim Regional Educational Attendance Area Lower Yukon Regional Educational Attendance Area Northwest Arctic Borough. The SEOC continues transitioning from response to recovery activity. Coordination with other federal, state, local, and tribal agencies is ongoing; delivering critical supplies and addressing other needs as presented. This includes performing detailed damage assessments to homes and repairs to critical infrastructure such as water, power, and communications in the impacted area as winterization becomes a concern. Statewide operations focus on stabilization, recovery, and winterization across the Y-K Delta and other impacted regions. Department of Transportation is prioritizing residential damage assessments in coordination with multiple agencies. They are implementing a standardized digital assessment process to reduce duplication and improve situational awareness. Department of Environmental Conservation staff and Remote Maintenance Workers have been on the ground, traveling between communities to help restore the systems that protect health and the environment — drinking water, wastewater, and fuel storage. As of this afternoon, 1,063 applications for state Individual Assistance (IA) have been received. Survivors in designated disaster areas may register for the State of Alaska’s Individual Assistance program: 2 • Online: https://ready.alaska.gov/ia • By phone: 1-844-445-7131 The state IA program provides financial assistance for damages to primary residences, vehicles, essential personal property, and medical, funeral, or dental needs directly resulting from the declared disaster. Individuals who are impacted by the disaster and are not staying at either shelter in Anchorage are encouraged to register for the state’s IA program to begin registration for long-term housing assistance. Congregate shelters remain open in Anchorage and Bethel. Additional survivors may be sheltering with neighbors, family, or friends in multiple communities. Last night, a total of 318 individuals were reported sheltering: Egan Center – 173, Alaska Airlines Center – 140 – Bethel 5. The State of Alaska Disaster Housing Task Force continues to meet daily to identify the next steps toward longer term non-congregate housing. The intent is to transition those impacted by the disaster into non-congregate housing as soon as reasonably possible. It is crucial that those who are impacted by the recent storms register for both state Individual Assistance and federal Individual Assistance as well as begin the process of registration for housing. Pets continue to go to shelters in Anchorage and Mat-Su. Reunification with their owners is the primary goal. Evacuees can contact the shelters below to find out if their dog is there. Mat-Su Animal Shelter: 907-746-5500 or 907-761-7501 Anchorage Shelter: 907-343-8138 If you have a dog that did not evacuate with you, text a picture to the Bethel Friends of Canines at 907-707-7010, and the staff will contact you. Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium is continuing to accept donations of traditional foods at the Alaska Native Medical Center and is providing subsistence-based meals for shelter residents along with medical support. There are 24 active missions under the Emergency Management Assistance Compact (EMAC) with participation from 13 states providing emergency management, public assistance, individual assistance and logistics personnel. A list of resources related to the disaster is available at ready.alaska.gov, under Top News. Interagency Partner Operations Alaska Organized Militia (AKOM): AKOM has 135 members activated on State Active Duty with additional authorization as needed for disaster response. In cooperation with Alaska Division of Forestry and Fire Prevention, crews are continuing to perform muck outs and home repairs. Three task forces remain active, conducting land, air, and sea missions across the Y–K Delta. 3 American Red Cross: Overnight, the Red Cross sheltered 173 individuals at the Egan Center, 140 at the Alaska Airlines Center, and 5 in Bethel. Anchorage School District (ASD): As of October 23, 2025 ASD reports approximately 140 students have enrolled in the ASD system and school bus service is being provided from the shelters to schools with Yup’ik immersion programs. ASD is continuing to provide bus services between shelters, neighborhood recreation centers, and schools. Association of Village Council Presidents (AVCP): AVCP is continuing to work with Yukon-Kuskokwim Health Corporation to conduct detailed community assessments, support home repairs, coordinate debris removal, and assist with collection of IA applications efforts in affected YK Delta communities. Staff from AVCP are available at the Anchorage shelters for assistance with Tribal ID cards. AVCP plans to hire 50 local workers for home repairs, including 10 crew bosses and a mix of laborers and carpenters. Priority hiring focuses on in-community applicants, with additional emergency hires from Kipnuk. Yukon-Kuskokwim Health Corporation (YKHC): YKHC crews are actively working in Kwigillingok and Kongiganak. Kipnuk clinic teams will remain through October 27th. YKHC completed water-system repairs in Kipnuk and redeployed to Bethel. Recovery teams are restoring water service, testing for contamination, and repairing fuel lines, wells, and damaged access roads. ### Media Contact: Public Information Officer News Desk 907-428-7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov

full_text: For Immediate Release April 26, 2022 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: Jeremy Zidek, 907-441-2337 River Watch to monitor Alaska river breakup and provide ice-jam flood warning Break-up flood potential above average due to high snow load, cold temperatures, and thick river ice JOINT BASE ELMENDORF-RICHARDSON, Alaska – Due to above average snow fall, infrequent thaw/freeze episodes and thick, in-place ice, the ice-jam flood potential for several interior Alaskan rivers is above average this spring. The Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management has a long-running partnership with the National Weather Service Alaska-Pacific River Forecast Center, coordinated through the Alaska State Emergency Operations Center, to monitor ice-jam conditions and provide timely updates to riverine communities. The partnership, known as River Watch, provides updates through real-time aerial surveillance in order to issue on-scene flood advisories and warnings, assist communities with flood preparations, and support emergency response operations if flooding occurs. “We see some type of flooding each and every spring, but conditions this year require extra preparation based on current conditions. Only time will tell where flooding occurs and how severe the inundation is, so every community should be prepared,” said Mark Roberts, SEOC River Watch incident commander. “In addition, the large amount of snow could cause spring flooding not associated with an ice jam.” Ice-jam flooding occurs when large pieces of intact ice stop moving in the river and create a dam. These ice jams can back up water for miles and spill over the banks far inland. Deep flood waters and massive hunks of ice can flood low-lying areas and cause serious community damage. SEOC, in coordination with the NWS Alaska-Pacific River Forecast Center, are conducting calls with at- risk riverine communities to provide the latest information on river conditions and flood risk . SEOC is also engaged in active coordination with community flood response partners including the Tanana Chiefs Conference, Yukon-Kuskokwim Health Corporation, Bethel Search and Rescue, American Red Cross of Alaska, Salvation Army, and Alaska Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster. The Alaska Rescue Coordination Center has been briefed on conditions and will be prepared to deploy appropriate resources in case of a flood emergency. An Alaska Army National Guard aviation unit will be conducting its federal annual training requirements in the western region from April 30 to May 12 and will be available to provide emergency support to the River Watch effort as requested by the Rescue Coordination Center. Air crews will train with four Black Hawk helicopters based out of Bethel and three Black Hawks based out of Nome. Both locations will have hoist capable aircraft in order to support a wide range of emergency rescue scenarios. Up-to-date river forecast information can be found at the Alaska River Forecast Center website https://www.weather.gov/aprfc/. ###

full_text: Fact Sheet Contact: Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Individual Assistance IA Hotline:1-844-445-7131 Online: Ready.Alaska.Gov DISASTER ASSISTANCE FOR INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES When the Governor declares a disaster and authorizes Individual Assistance, Alaska’s Individual and Family Grant (IFG) Program and Temporary Housing Program (THP) provide timely assistance to individuals or families to meet disaster-related necessary expenses and serious needs. Together, these programs provide essential support when other resources are unavailable or inadequate. The Individual Assistance program works closely with disaster-affected communities to ensure applicants are aware of the available IA resources. Individuals apply with the Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management (DHS & EM) for 60 days following declaration of a disaster via: • Telephone. Register call 1-844-445-7131. You may be asked to leave a message with contact information. A DHS&EM Individual Assistance staff member will call you back shortly. • Online. Register online at Ready.Alaska.Gov. To expedite the process, have proof of ownership and insurance documents ready to submit. A list of damaged items and photographs will help expedite the process. IA staff work closely with individuals on their eligibility applications and throughout the program to ensure the most assistance possible is given. Applicants are required to spend funds appropriately and to document expenditures. I NDIVIDUAL AND F AMILY G RANT (IFG) P ROGRAM The current maximum grant to an individual or family is $21,400 for housing repair and an additional $21,400 for personal property damages per disaster when other resources are not adequate, including insurance and Small Business Association (SBA) or other loans. Assistance can include: • Housing (primary residences only). Money to repair, replace, or rebuild; provide access; clean or make sanitary; remove debris relating to life- health- and safety-issues; protective against immediate threat. • Personal property. Money to replace essential clothing; household items, furnishings or appliances; tools and employer-required specialized clothing; subsistence equipment or structures; repair, cleaning or sanitizing of personal property; or moving and storage to prevent or reduce further damage. • Transportation. Money to ensure one primary vehicle remains in operation. • Medical and Dental Expenses. Money to pay for disaster-related medical and dental care or equipment. • Funeral Expenses. Money for funeral and burial/cremation expenses related to a disaster-related death. T EMPORARY H OUSING P ROGRAM The Temporary Housing Program provides timely assistance to individuals or families displaced from their primary residence as a result of the disaster. Assistance can include: • Transient accommodations. Immediate short-term housing; may include shelters, families, and friends. • Rent and eligible utilities. Initial rental assistance is 90 days for renters and 18 months for home owners. Additional assistance may continue as part of a permanent housing plan. • Repair and replacement of the damaged primary residence in situations where restoring the essential living areas is less than providing other forms of temporary housing assistance.

full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE November 1, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information News Desk 907- 428-7142, Jeremy.Zidek@Alaska.gov SEOC Update: 2025 October West Coast Storm – Disaster Update JOINT BASE ELMENDORF RICHARDSON, Alaska — A Major Disaster Declaration has been signed by President Trump in response to a state-declared disaster, for the 2025 October West Coast Storms, including Typhoon Halong and related storms. The State Emergency Operations Center (SEOC) is coordinating with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to transition from a state-led response to a joint, long-term recovery operation through a Unified Command. The primary focus is life sustainment and stabilization for the impacted area. Recovery is a priority for the impacted areas, and recovery operations continue with an emphasis on restoring critical infrastructure and services – including water, power, and communications, and emergency home and boardwalk repairs. Coordination between federal, state, local and tribal partners is continuing to provide critical supplies to impacted communities and address community needs as they are reported. As of this afternoon, 1,206 applications for state Individual Assistance (IA) have been received. FEMA has received 378 IA applications to date. State IA and FEMA IA are coordinating to share information and encourage applicants register for each program. All individuals residing in congregate shelters in Anchorage and Bethel have transitioned to non-congregate sheltering, some shelters will remain in standby status for the coming days to accept potential evacuees. Some survivors may be sheltering with neighbors, family, or friends; it is crucial that those who are affected by the recent storms register for both state and federal IA programs and other forms of assistance. full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE October 24, 2025 Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Media Contact: State Emergency Operation Center Public Information Desk 907-428-7142, or Jeremy.Zidek@alaska.gov Give Wisely: Ensuring Your Disaster Donations Make a Real Difference Joint Base ELMENDORF Richardson, Alaska – In the wake of the recent Alaska West Coast Storm, many people feel the urgent desire to help those aﬀected. Financial donations are often the most eﬀective way to support disaster response and recovery—but only when given to legitimate organizations. Unfortunately, scam operations often appear during times of crisis, preying on the generosity of well-intentioned donors. To ensure your donation truly helps those in need, follow these tips for giving safely and eﬀectively: 1. Donate to Established, Recognized Organizations Choose reputable disaster relief organizations with a proven track record, such as: • The American Red Cross • The Salvation Army • Food Bank of Alaska • World Central Kitchen • Faith-based organizations known for disaster response eﬀorts such as Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster (VOAD) Team Rubicon continues to manage donations. Priority items remain the following: Used items are not requested at this time • Winter Coats: adults and children, all sizes • Winter Boots: adults and children, all sizes • Camping mattress pads • Sleeping bags • Blankets – twin, full and queen sizes • Luggage including duﬄe bags 2 • New, with tags clothing for adults (XS – 5XL) • New, with tags clothing for children (all sizes) • New shoes (including slip-ons and slides) • New winter hats and gloves • Personal hygiene items (soap, shampoo/conditioner, deodorant, lotion, hairbrushes/combs, hair ties, nail clippers, lip balm, etc.) A Team Rubicon distribution center is at 1120 East 1st Avenue. Goods are being moved in and out daily to support survivors staying in shelters and those visiting shelters for assistance. Donations can be dropped oﬀ 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily To donate ﬁnancial support to Team Rubicon, go to https://teamrubiconusa.org/ The Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium (ANTHC) is accepting subsistence and traditional food donations to provide nourishing meals for the families displaced to Anchorage. Bring donations to ANTHC Lodging at Tudor Centre, 4001 Tudor Centre Drive, Monday-Friday from 9am to 4pm. https://anthc.org/ Several local community organizations and regional partners have come together to establish the Western Alaska Disaster Relief Fund through the Alaska Community Foundation. Donate to the fund through the Alaska Community Foundation website at https://alaskacf.org/ The American Red Cross of Alaska, Salvation Army Alaska Division, World Central Kitchen, Alaska Food Bank, and other Alaska VOADs are all contributing to the disaster response and are accepting donations which can be used for storm response. 2. Verify Before You Give Before donating, verify that the charity is legitimate by visiting trusted sources such as: • Charity Navigator • Give.org Resource Links • Alaska VOAD • Donation Video • FEMA Donation Video 3. Be Cautious with Online Campaigns Crowdfunding and social media fundraisers can be powerful tools—but not all are veriﬁed. Before contributing: 3 • Conﬁrm that the campaign lists a speciﬁc organization or individual you can identify. • Look for transparency about how funds will be used. • Be wary of urgent or emotional appeals that lack clear details. 4. Don’t Give to Unsolicited Requests Be skeptical of unexpected emails, texts, or phone calls asking for donations. Scammers often use fake names or create look-alike websites. Always go directly to an organization’s oﬃcial website rather than following links in messages or posts. 5. Give Money, Not Supplies—Unless Requested For information on how to donate or for survivors to access donations, please see the resource flyer available on our website: Resource Flyer 6. Report Fraud to the Disaster Fraud Hotline If you have knowledge of fraud, waste, abuse, or allegations of mismanagement involving disaster relief operations. Call the Disaster Fraud Hotline at 866-720-5721, or go to Justice.gov/DisasterComplaintForm, Or write: National Center for Disaster Fraud, Baton Rouge, LA 70821-4909 Calls can be made anonymously and conﬁdentially ### END ###

full_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE April 27, 2021 Contact: Jeremy Zidek (907) 441-2337 River Watch teams prepared to launch as river break-up begins River Watch teams conduct river breakup observation and provide early warning to residents JOINT BASE ELMENDORF-RICHARDSON, Alaska – The State of Alaska Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management (DHS&EM) is assisting communities in preparation for breakup along Alaska’s major river systems this spring. Breakup is a time of both excitement and anxiety. Residents anticipate the ability to travel along the rivers, but are also concerned with the threat that ice jam flooding poses to their communities. Each spring the River Watch program renews a partnership between DHS&EM and the National Weather Service (NWS). The Alaska-Pacific River Forecast Center (APRFC) and DHS&EM conduct aerial observations of rivers prone to ice jam flooding. The team provides flood warnings and assists communities responding to flood emergencies. The River Watch partnership has existed for more than 30 years. The first River Watch team is planning to begin surveillance flights on the Upper Yukon and Kuskokwim Rivers the first week of May. The Alaska Pacific River Forecast Center has updated their spring flood outlook based on river ice thickness, snowpack, and climate outlooks. The Kuskokwim, Upper Yukon River, and rivers along Turnagain Arm, Gulf of Alaska, and northern Southeast Panhandle are considered above average; the Tanana, remainder of the Yukon River, and Copper Rivers are considered average, and the North Slope and Koyukuk Rivers are considered below average. “We take the above average river flooding very seriously. We are communicating with communities in all areas to make them aware of the flood potential, encouraging communities to take steps to prepare for flooding, and readying our response partners so the state can act quickly if flooding occurs,” said Bryan Fisher, DHS&EM acting director. “As we have for many years, River Watch will be in place to provide up-to-date flood information to communities, and help respond if flooding occurs.” This year, due to COVID-19 concerns, the River Watch team may or may not land in some communities. All COVID-19 safety protocols will be in effect where River Watch teams land, such as wearing masks, and social distancing. If a community asks for a River Watch team not to land, the team will provide the same observations and warning services via VHF radio as they fly over the community. Currently, River Watch is conducting a series of teleconferences with partners and river communities along the Yukon and Kuskokwim Rivers. An Alaska Army National Guard hoist-capable UH-60 Black Hawk helicopter is traveling to Bethel today as part of the State’s effort to prepare for disaster response in the Yukon-Kuskokwim region during the spring flood season. They will continue their regular federal mission training while in Bethel, ready to respond to the State upon request. A Black Hawk aircrew is equipped and prepared to respond expeditiously to a rapid event that may require evacuation. This year’s breakup forecast may be found at http://www.weather.gov/aprfc/floodpotential Break up map at https://www.weather.gov/aprfc/breakupMap ###

Torrence Saxe Commissioner & Adjutant General Department of Military and Veterans Affairs www.DMVA.Alaska.Gov STATE OF ALASKA OF ALASKA Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska PRESS RELEASE FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE March 3, 2021 Contact: Jeremy Zidek (907) 441-2337 DHS&EM Working with Unalakleet to Restore Water Service JOINT BASE ELMENDORF-RICHARDSON, Alaska - The City of Unalakleet issued a local disaster declaration on Feb. 26, after a combination of wind and extreme cold weather resulted in power outages, and damage to the community's water distribution system. Currently, the community has sources of drinking water and is taking water conservation measures. The Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management (DHS&EM) has been in communication with Unalakleet's mayor and city manager. Unalakleet's water supply relies on a four-mile-long distribution line from the Powers Creek source to the city's one million gallon water storage tank. Frozen distribution lines and limited water availability have diminished resident's water service. Continued efforts to thaw the frozen lines and fix breaks in distribution lines have been taking place. In addition, DHS&EM is working with the Norton Sound Health Corporation and the Department of Environmental Conservation's (DEC) Remote Maintenance Worker Program, which addresses water issues in rural Alaska. The multiagency group will continue work with the community to assess the condition of the community's water system and restore normal water service. The State Emergency Operation Center stands ready to address emergency needs if they arise. The community arranged delivery from a water supply at an elder care facility in Unalakleet for those without access to potable water or have the means to transport water. In addition, residents are utilizing private wells in the community as a source of potable water. "The City of Unalakleet's water system is old and has needed to be upgraded for many years," said DHS&EM Director Paul Nelson. "While replacing old infrastructure is not eligible under the state's Public Assistance program, we can and will address critical life, health and safety needs like access to potable water. We can take action with or without a disaster declaration." DEC issued a boil water notice for water from the City of Unalakleet's water system due to multiple freeze-ups and line breaks in the distribution system. The community is seeking funding to establish a process to utilize new wells in the community that are not yet connected to the existing water system. ### ---PAGE---

event_description: AVCP-TH Partnership (12/11/2025)
